sn28.1:1.1: Sāriputta, personal name Upatissa ([mn24:17.3]()), was the greatest disciple of the Buddha, foremost in wisdom ([an1.189]()), the “general of the Dhamma” ([ud2.8:16.2]()) who was “like unto the Teacher himself” ([mn24:17.5]()). He is known for his magnificent expositions of fundamental teachings ([mn9](), [mn141]()), his ready conversation on profound matters ([mn24](), [mn43]()), his careful guidance for fellow monastics ([mn5]()), and his personal qualities of gentleness and forgiveness. His verses are at [thag17.2]().
